references.text: The description of the peace offering (shelamim) and its regulations, which form the basis for the peace offerings mentioned in Numbers 7:47
Detailed instructions on how the peace offering is to be performed and eaten
The same offerings from Nahshon, son of Amminadab, showing the repeated pattern of the tribal leaders' offerings
The same offerings from Netanel, son of Zuar, confirming the fixed pattern for the peace offering
The same offerings from Eliab, son of Helon, demonstrating continuity in the gifts of the tribal leaders
The same offerings from Elizur, son of Shedeur, with identical quantities of cattle, rams, male goats, and lambs
The same offerings from Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, which immediately precede Eliasaph's offering
Eliasaph, son of Deuel, is mentioned as the leader of the tribe of Gad in the census
Eliasaph, son of Deuel, identified as the commander over the army of the sons of Gad in the camp
